item.title: Self-Hosted Initramfs Builders: dracut vs mkinitcpio vs initramfs-tools
item.description: When a Linux server boots, the kernel needs access to the root filesystem — which may reside on LVM, encrypted volumes, RAID arrays, or network storage. The initramfs (initial RAM filesystem) bridges this gap by loading drivers, unlocking encrypted disks, and assembling storage before the real root mounts. But not all initramfs builders are created equal.
